$comment: Inputs for tools/season_from_research.py: maps the 2013 entrants to pack teams, colours and tracks. Rules, car profiles, engines and tyres come from the era base (bases/dtm-era4/gen.json).
title: DTM 2013 - Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters

Audi Sport Team Phoenix.history: Founded by Ernst Moser. Based in Meuspath, next to the Nürburgring. Has run Audis in the DTM since 2006.

BMW Team RBM.history: Founded by Bart Mampaey. Based in Mechelen, Belgium. Has run BMWs in the DTM since 2012.

STIHL AMG-Mercedes.history: Run by HWA AG from Affalterbach. HWA builds and runs the Mercedes DTM cars. One of two HWA teams in 2013.

BMW Team Schnitzer.history: Based in Freilassing. Has raced BMWs since the 1960s. Bruno Spengler won the 2012 title with the team.

entrants: Audi Sport Team Abt Sportsline [Abt Sportsline]
Audi Sport Team Abt Sportsline.history: Hans-Jürgen Abt's team from Kempten. Has run Audis in the DTM since 2000. Mattias Ekström won the title with the team in 2004 and 2007.

Euronics AMG-Mercedes.history: The second HWA AG team, entered as EURONICS/Thomas Sabo AMG-Mercedes. Gary Paffett won the 2005 title.

BMW Team MTEK.history: Ernest Knoors' team from the Netherlands. New to the DTM in 2013. Drivers are former Formula 1 driver Timo Glock and rookie Marco Wittmann.

Audi Sport Team Abt.history: The second Abt Sportsline team. Timo Scheider won the title in 2008 and 2009. Adrien Tambay is in his second DTM season.

stern AMG-Mercedes.history: Peter Mücke's team from Berlin. Runs Mercedes cars. Both drivers come from Formula 3.

entrants: BMW Team RMG [Reinhold Motorsport / Team RMG]
BMW Team RMG.history: Stefan Reinhold's team from Andernach. Has run BMWs in the DTM since 2012. Martin Tomczyk won the 2011 title.

Audi Sport Team Rosberg.history: Keke Rosberg's team from Neustadt an der Weinstraße. First DTM season in 1995 with Opel. Raced Mercedes from 2000 to 2004 and Audi since 2006.

sponsors.$comment: Starting deals from the 2013 liveries (research/spotter_guide.csv, research/liveries.csv), primary first: the lower-numbered car's main sponsor, then the team-mate's, then partners on the team's cars. Each sponsor is on one team only, so make-wide partners (Puma, Sonax, Würth...) are spread over that make's teams. The manufacturers' own campaigns (bmw.com/m3, AMG, Audi ultra, Audi Cup) and the series partners (DEKRA, ADAC, Hankook) are left out. Names are used descriptively only, no logos. build_pack.py keeps each team's sponsor income at what its cloned vanilla team had.

juniors.$comment: Feeder series from research/juniors/<id>_*.csv (tools/season_from_research.py juniors()). The game runs one race per series and week, so a weekend counts as one race. skill_range and quality_range set the ratings from the 2013 points; licence_start gives the starting licence points (x share of the champion's points).

free_agents.$comment: Hand-rated free agents from research/juniors/free_agents.csv (DTM skills run 11-18). Ex-F1 drivers without a 2013 race seat, and Red Bull juniors. Kept few: the game favours free agents.

series.name: FIA Formula 3 European Championship
series.description: The European Formula 3 championship. Dallara cars with Mercedes, Volkswagen and Toyota engines. It races at most DTM weekends, and several DTM drivers came from here.

series.name: Porsche Carrera Cup Deutschland
series.description: A one-make cup with the Porsche 911 GT3 Cup. It races at DTM weekends. Young professionals race here on their way to GT and touring car seats.

series.name: ATS Formel 3 Cup
series.description: The German Formula 3 championship. Smaller teams and a Trophy class for older cars. It races at ADAC GT Masters weekends.

series.name: ADAC Formel Masters
series.description: A single-seater series for teenagers stepping up from karting. All drivers use the same Dallara car with a Volkswagen engine. It races at ADAC GT Masters weekends.

series.name: Deutsche Tourenwagen Challenge
series.description: The ADAC Procar series for production-based touring cars. Super 2000 and Super 1600 cars race in two divisions at ADAC GT Masters weekends. From 2016 it was called Deutscher Tourenwagen Cup.
